title: Special operators: overflow checks, nameof, and sizeof
hook: Three operators that look small but save you in interviews and production: checked makes integer overflow throw, nameof gives you a rename-safe string of a symbol, and sizeof reports the byte size of an unmanaged value type.

sections.heading: What are checked, nameof, and sizeof?

blocks.text: The **checked** context makes integer arithmetic throw OverflowException instead of silently wrapping around. **nameof** is a compile-time operator that returns the string name of a variable, type, or member — it survives rename refactoring. **sizeof** returns the size in bytes of an unmanaged value type at compile time. None of these are like JavaScript typeof — nameof is evaluated at compile time, and sizeof only works on value types, not objects on the heap.

entries.plainDefinition: A region or expression where integer overflow throws OverflowException instead of wrapping silently.
entries.example: int n = checked(int.MaxValue + 1); // throws instead of wrapping to MinValue.

entries.plainDefinition: A compile-time operator that returns the unqualified string name of a symbol. Rename-safe when you use an IDE refactor.
entries.example: nameof(RetryCount) returns "RetryCount" even after you rename the field.

entries.plainDefinition: Returns the size in bytes of an unmanaged value type. Not the garbage-collected heap size of an object.
entries.example: sizeof(int) is 4. sizeof(string) is a compile error — string is a reference type.

sections.heading: Why these operators matter in production

blocks.text: Use checked when a count of concurrent attempts must not silently wrap from int.MaxValue back to int.MinValue. Use nameof in exception messages and log keys so renaming a field does not leave stale string literals behind. As of C# 14, nameof(List<>) returns "List" — you no longer need a dummy List<int> just to name an open generic type. sizeof is for interop and low-level buffer sizing with unmanaged structs, not for measuring object memory (that is module 14).

blocks.title: Default is unchecked
blocks.body: By default, int arithmetic wraps in an unchecked context. Project-wide checked arithmetic is an MSBuild property (CheckForOverflowUnderflow). Most Base Class Library (BCL) code assumes unchecked wraparound.

blocks.title: checked, nameof, and sizeof at compile time

items.title: checked evaluates at run time
items.body: The compiler emits overflow checks. If the result exceeds the type range, OverflowException is thrown.

items.title: nameof resolves at compile time
items.body: The compiler replaces nameof(X) with the string "X". No reflection, no run-time cost.

items.title: sizeof resolves at compile time
items.body: Returns a constant integer for unmanaged value types. Requires unsafe context for custom structs in some cases.

sections.heading: Code walkthrough: overflow, names, and sizes

snippet.label: checked overflow versus default wrap
snippet.explanation: Use checked when silent wraparound would corrupt a counter or window calculation.

snippet.label: nameof for rename-safe strings
snippet.explanation: nameof survives IDE rename refactoring. C# 14 allows unbound generics: nameof(List<>) is "List" without inventing List<int>.

snippet.label: sizeof for unmanaged value types
snippet.explanation: sizeof is a compile-time constant for unmanaged value types. It is not the garbage-collected heap size of an object.

blocks.title: C# vs JavaScript/TypeScript
rows: IEEE-754 numbers do not wrap like int32
typeof x returns runtime type string
No sizeof; use ArrayBuffer for binary

blocks.title: Top pitfalls
blocks.body: Using typeof(List<>).Name in older code when nameof(List<>) is now legal and clearer. Assuming sizeof equals the memory a SkiaSharp bitmap occupies — it does not. Wrapping a whole service in checked and surprising yourself on GetHashCode-style math. Using sizeof on a class or string — compile error.

interviewTakeaways: Default arithmetic is unchecked wraparound unless you opt into checked.
nameof is compile-time and rename-safe; C# 14 allows unbound generics like List<>.
sizeof applies to unmanaged value types, not class instances.
checked throws OverflowException; unchecked wraps silently.
commonPitfalls: Using typeof(List<>).Name in older code when nameof(List<>) is now legal and clearer.
Assuming sizeof equals memory a SkiaSharp bitmap occupies — it does not.
Wrapping a whole service in checked and surprising yourself on GetHashCode-style math.
Confusing nameof (compile-time string) with typeof (runtime Type object).

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript numbers are IEEE-754; they do not wrap like int32. typeof is runtime. C# nameof is compile-time; sizeof is a constant for unmanaged types.
